name: smwpatches-all-in-one-multiple-death-songs-1
title: All-in-one Multiple Death Songs 1.0
description:
This patch allows you to have multiple death songs using various logics: per-level, per-world, randomized, per-player... or even all of them! (in this order of priority)
See .asm file for more details.

Important note: AMK users, be wary of the original songs order change. In addition, to ensure your custom music causes no pause, be sure to insert at as a global song. Also, you'll need to remove a hijack in Tweaks.asm so you don't need to reapply this patch each time you use AMK!

Requested by Daizo Dee Von.

name: smwpatches-better-random-number-generator
title: Better Random Number Generator
description:
This patch will replace SMW's RNG with a faster, shorter, and more random number generator. It will also let you use $148B and $148C as freeram. Requires no freespace.

Note: Here are some optional routines that let you do a few advanced things with the RNG function.

name: smwpatches-bonus-stars-sum-game
title: Bonus Stars Sum Game
description:
This patch enables a game that can be played when a goal tape is collected. By pressing L or R during the goal march, you're able to input the resulting sum of bonus stars. If input correctly before the sum starts to roll, the player gets a 1-up. You can optionally add a punishment for a wrong answer.

Once active, the controls of the game are the following:
<, >, L or R = Swap the selected digit.
^ and v = Increase and decrease the selected digit, respectively.
A and B = Increase and decrease the ones digit, respectively.
X and Y = Increase and decrease the tens digit, respectively.

An optional UberASM level code is included to change the palette of the numbers while the game is active, though it is only compatible with the vanilla status bar.

name: smwpatches-bounce-block-fixes-v1-2
title: Bounce block fixes v1.2.2
description:
This patch fixes various bounce block-related glitches:
  • Blocks can be hit multiple times before turning into tile $152 briefly, either by multiple kicked sprites hitting the block at the same frame, or during $9D being set. SMW only lets the block change via processing the bounce sprite, rather than immidiately.
  • The flip kicked sprite effect reuses the quake effect, causing sprites to always be knocked away from the player, even when the block is hit by a kicked sprite from the opposite side of the player


Changelog
Code
8/7/2025 - 1.2.1 - The depreciation warning update + modernized tools to use.
	-Fixed a depreciation warning (order of operations to invert a number: X^$FF+1 is
	 now (X^$FF)+1)
	-Renamed "GM14.asm" to "GM14_BounceFlipSpr.asm" to make it easy for the user to
	 recognize what it is.
	-Made custom block routine to use macro labels to avoid leaking sublabels.
	-Make use of bank $80 when not using SA-1 for fastROM.
2-28-2026 - 1.2.2
	-Fixed an issue where SA-1's hijack at $02887D conflicts with this patch's hijack
	 at $02887A, causing the game to crash when the bounceable blocks are triggered.
	-Fixed an erroneous code where the init for uberasm tool only clearing the bounce
	 sprite's X low position when it was meant to clear out all its slot data on level
	 load.
	 -Renamed several defines and folders to reduce the risk of naming conflicts.
	-Changed "BounceBlocksFixDef.txt" to "BounceBlocksFixDef.asm"
	-Due to an update on UAT2.0, which allows multiple ASM resources on levels,
	 this made reliance on GM14 redundant.

name: smwpatches-carry-items-through-doors-and-diagonal-pipes
title: Carry Items Through Doors and Diagonal Pipes
description:
Enables the player to be able to carry items through doors.

Also fixes the player dropping carried items when shooting out of a diagonal pipe.

versions.title: Carry Items Through Doors and Diagonal Pipes
versions.filename: Carry Items Through Doors and Diagonal Pipes.zip

name: smwpatches-chuck-breaking-blocks-fix
title: Chuck Breaking Blocks Fix
description:
Did you notice that, when chucks break through turn/throw blocks, the brick piece particles are always rainbow? Except, it turns out that isn't always the case, as the code that handles this is bugged. It uses the block's X/Y position to determine whether the brick pieces are rainbow or not. This causes one of the blocks to create non-rainbow particles when they're placed on the first screen of the level.

This patch fixes both of these quirks. With this, turn blocks will always create brown particles and throw blocks will always create rainbow particles when chucks smash through them.

Credit is not required, but appreciated.

name: smwpatches-collected-moon-outline
title: Collected Moon Outline
description:
Makes a "collected" tile appear once a moon is collected. That tile will also appear in place of the moon when the room is reentered.

The sample graphics seen in the .gif are included.

name: smwpatches-course-clear-modifier
title: "Course Clear" Modifier
description: This patch allows you to change the "Course Clear!" text and some other text at the end of the level to what you want. The patch is largely commented.

name: smwpatches-custom-end-level-stars-text
title: Custom End Level Stars Text
description:
This patch will change what's displayed when touching the goal tape: instead of showing the number of bonus stars rewarded, it'll display a custom text (by default, "GG"). It's fairly easy to change what will be displayed or add more characters. There's also an option to show the text even if not grabbing the goal tape, but this is recommended to use only if bonus stars are disabled in the hack (since with this option they would be rewarded even if not touching the goal tape).
Check the asm file for more info.

name: smwpatches-different-values-for
title: Different Values for 1-Up
description:
Leverages unused Super Mario World code to allow you to set a different lives value for 1-up mushrooms, when the extra bit is set and using extra byte 1, without using a custom sprite slot. You can also remap the tile and the palette!

Requires PIXI to work. Requires five bytes of free ROM in bank 01.

name: smwpatches-display-disclaimer-message-on-boot
title: Display Disclaimer Message on Boot
description:
This patch allows you to display a message, intended as a disclaimer, on boot. Can be useful for, say, epilepsy warnings or emulator issues.

Message can be displayed always or when a condition is met. If set to be conditional, it defaults to allowing the user to continue, but this can be changed.

By default, it shows a warning screen if you try to run the hack under (Super) ZSNES.

name: smwpatches-dma-remap-v3
title: DMA Remap v3.0
description:
Remaps the default channels used by DMA in Super Mario World, allocating these transfers to the first three channels and giving you five HDMA channels free for you to use outside of the credits roll.

By default, the remaps are the following:
  • Channel 0 is reserved for DMAs outside interrupts.
  • Channel 1 is reserved for the vanilla windowing HDMA.
  • Channel 2 is reserved for DMAs in interrupts.
  • You can use channels 3 to 7 for HDMA effects.


This patch is included in SA-1 Pack and re-patching it is not needed if you have that, but it could help LoROM users should they need more HDMA channels.

name: smwpatches-dry-bones-and-bony-beetle-suboffscreen-fix
title: Dry Bones and Bony Beetle SubOffScreen Fix
description: Fixes an oversight that caused Dry Bones and Bony Beetle to not despawn offscreen if they're in their crumbled state, until they revive. This is because such subroutine is only called in their "normal" state.

versions.title: Dry Bones and Bony Beetle SubOffScreen Fix

name: smwpatches-enemy-credit-sprite-changer-with-graphical-fix
title: Enemy Credit Sprite Changer (With Graphical Fix)
description:
Added a bit more documentation, Thank lx5 for that.

Do you want to change some of the original ending's enemy sprite data without fuss? This should be the patch for the job, Included is a oversight fix regarding palette and tile data in the original enemy ending data.

Enjoy.

versions.title: Enemy Credit Sprite Changer (With Graphical Fix)

name: smwpatches-enter-level-pipe-star-road-sounds-v1
title: Enter Level/Pipe/Star Road Sounds v1.1
description:
This patch makes the game play a sound effect when you enter levels and use pipes from the overworld (much like in SMB3) while also including the ability to change the sound star roads use for their warping shenanigans for the sake of convenience.

SFX to be played for each tile is customizeable in the ASM file.

1.1: Fixes a crash caused when using an Overworld Warp Pipe in a rom with BOWSIE applied.

name: smwpatches-fade-in-pack
title: Fade-in Pack
description:
These two patches change the game's default mosaic fade-in to either a circle that zooms into or out from the player or a "horizontally convex" shape that zooms into or out from the center of the screen.

Mod Note: If you happen to be using HDMA that messes with the layer 1 X/Y position ($210D-$210E), the shape fade, and you're not using the SA-1 patch, the HDMA will mess with random scanlines of the fade effect. This is minor and likely won't affect most SMW hacks, but will be mentioned here in the rare case it comes up.

name: smwpatches-fix-camera-during-goal-walk-and-pipe-entry
title: Fix Camera During Goal Walk and Pipe Entry
description:
This patch fixes a niche bug where the camera jitters and doesn't scroll forwards properly during the goal walk or when the player's entering a horizontal pipe, occurring when the camera is scrolled away from the direction the player is walking. This happens because part of the camera's code that is found in the L/R scrolling routine doesn't run during the goal walk or when entering pipes - this patch fixes that.

If you have previously disabled L/R scrolling, this patch will reanable it (a side effect of my implementation), but an option to disable L/R scrolling can be found inside of the file. Patch with that option enabled if you wish to have the scrolling disabled.

Should be compatible with Burning Loaf's Alternative + Vertical L/R Scrolling patch, HOWEVER a few things to note: My patch should be applied after Loaf's patch, and a minor modification needs to be made to his, otherwise the player will be able to scroll the camera with L and R during the goal walk:
Show me it
An 
ORA $1493|!addr
should be added below line 157 of the asm file, like so:
Code
.controllerCheck
	LDA $1401|!addr     ;\ $1401 remains unused,
	AND #$01            ;|
	ORA $1493|!addr  ; (this line is the one that was added)
	BNE .updateCam      ;/ so now it's a disable L/R scrolling flag instead

versions.title: Fix Camera During Goal Walk and Pipe Entry

name: smwpatches-free-roaming-overworld
title: Free Roaming Overworld
description:
This patch will allow the player to move freely on the overworld originally inspired by the Super Mario 3D world overworld.

I made this patch about 5-6 months ago and since someone requested it I decided to actually upload this.

Note that layer 1 path tiles (Including warp tiles) are removed. Use pipes and stars to warp between maps.
Also note that star warps need to have a level other than 0 or they won't work. (Yes that's intentional)

Update:
- Fixed save prompts
- Fixed issues with second player

(Requested by TrashCan64)

name: smwpatches-freeze-timer-with-string
title: Freeze Timer With String
description: Makes the game timer display a string upon reaching a certain timer value.

name: smwpatches-kick-and-drop-override-fix
title: Kick and Drop Override Fix
description: This simple patch fixes a bug that happens if you kick or drop a Bob-Omb the same frame it explodes, and a similar thing with custom blocks that would fail to delete a carried sprite the same frame the player kicks or drop a sprite.

name: smwpatches-koopaling-palette-changer
title: Koopaling Palette Changer
description:
This patch allows the user to easily change the palette all seven Koopalings use.

Credit is not required.

versions.title: Koopaling Palette Changer
versions.filename: SMW Koopaling Palette Changer Patch V1.1.zip

name: smwpatches-limited-yoshi-flying
title: Limited Yoshi Flying
description:
This patch will prevent yoshi with blue shell from flying forever and ever.

limitation of flight is configurable.

fixed bugs and with SA-1 support.

name: smwpatches-line-guide-acts-like-fix
title: Line Guide Acts Like Fix
description:
This patch makes the line guide processsing routine use the "acts like" setting instead of the Map16 number. This makes it possible to use ExGFX for line guides without worrying about where the tiles are in the Map16 pages.

worldpeace's note
The vanilla code of line guide interaction sometimes tries to restore the sprite's position from backup RAM, even if they aren't properly stored. This results in teleportation of line-guided sprites. (Like other vanilla glitches, this has been regarded as a feature and utilized for vanilla tricks!)

The previous version assumed the correctness of Nintendo's code however, and accessed some invalid "acts like" values as a result. It caused game freezing in some emulators (e.g. higan v092); for those who're interested, the patch got the map16 value outside of the level area and repeated a loop infinitely.

My version fixes the freezing issue, as well as giving some extra option regarding behaviors of line guide. You can choose the frequency of odd behaviors, which are the following:
1) Map16 tiles in the page 1 (or acting like one) work as "line guide end".
2) Those tiles let line-guided sprites teleport to certain position.

(These behaviors have already existed, and can be rarely observed in vanilla; only when the line-guided sprite is at a specific position which is decided by the map16 page of interacting tiles.)

This version also supports SA-1.

name: smwpatches-messagebox-in-minimalist-status-bar-goal-customizer
title: MessageBox in Minimalist Status Bar + Goal Customizer
description:
This patch combines the message box with the Minimalist Status Bar to allow Layer 3 effects and messages to coexist.
* It can coexist with layer 3 HDMA effects (Parallax, etc ...), and layer 3 water.
* It also disables goal messages and post-goal fades.
* No sprite tiles are used in the message field.
* It has custom message functions for selections, numerical inputs and name labels.
* The status bar is displayed correctly in Mode 7 boss battles.
* The HDMA effect will not be canceled even during the key goal and zooming circle.
* Compatible with LX5's Star Coins and Custom Powerups.
* Compatible with the Retry systems made by worldpeace and Kevin.

Includes sample patches and other sample files.

NOTES BEFORE PATCHING
NOTE: Before applying the patch, edit any of the levels and enable the standard Layer 3 tile map bypass for any level.

NOTE FOR SA-1 USERS: To use with the latest SA-1, open remap/dma.asm and replace !window_hdma_channel = 1 with 7 before applying.
Otherwise, problems will occur in the overworld and some other sections of the game.


Sample patch message box details
The message box in the sample hack uses this.
However, the code around line 76 is rewritten from
Code
	BEQ .default
	STA $13BF|!Base2
	LDA #$03
	STA !15AC,x
.default
	LDA !E4,x	; Load X position..
	LSR		; ..
	LSR		; ..
	LSR		; ..
	LSR		; ..
	AND #$01	; And make the sprite..
	INC		; Display its message..

to
Code
	STA $0F40|!Base2
	LDA #$00 ; !extra_byte_2,x
	STA $0F41|!Base2
	LDA #$04

versions.title: MessageBox in Minimalist Status Bar + Goal Customizer
versions.filename: Message in Minimalist Status Bar + Goal Customizer.zip

name: smwpatches-mode
title: Mode 3/8bpp Nintendo Presents Screen
description:
This patch enables Mode 3 for the Nintendo Presents screen, which means it allows you to put a 256 color picture as your Nintendo Presents screen.

Please read the enclosed README thoroughly to understand how to use this.

name: smwpatches-modified-bomber-banzai-bill-entrance
title: Modified Bomber/Banzai Bill Entrance
description:
This patch modifies the entrance Bomber/Banzai Bills make by adding a quake effect whenever it appears.

Credit's not required but heavily appreciated.

name: smwpatches-more-fireballs
title: More Fireballs
description:
This patch will allow you to shoot more than two fireballs, up to 10, in fact (though high values should be avoided when using other extended sprites or the mode 7 bosses).

Requires 10 bytes of freespace in bank $02.

name: smwpatches-morton-roy-ludwig-tilemap-editor
title: Morton, Roy & Ludwig Tilemap Editor
description:
This patch provides users an easy way to edit and remap Super Mario World's Morton, Roy and Ludwig's tilemap per pose, a troublesome endeavor normally due to theirs being rendered in Mode 7.

It also comes with two extra options that can be toggled on if the user wishes so:
1. The means to repurpose one of Ludwig's unused poses into a potential fourth shell pose.
2. An optional hijack that makes Morton & Roy switch poses when landing on the ground for their earthquake attack (requires freespace!).

Credit's not necessary, but very much appreciated.

name: smwpatches-multiple-title-screen-demos-v1-1
title: Multiple Title Screen Demos v1.1.2
description:
A patch that allows you to have multiple title screens, either chosen at random or in a set order. Allows up to 64. All of them have their own movement data!
Requested by Segment1Zone2.

I also made a tool to extract titlescreen recording moves from snes9x and Mesen 2 saves, assuming the LM hack is enabled. Get it here.

name: smwpatches-optimize
title: Optimize $0400 Compression Routine
description:
This patch optimizes the routine at $008494, which is run at the end of every frame to compress the $0420 table to $0400, saving 2 scanlines of processing on FastROM (if this patch is used, it'll save ~2.2 scanlines), at the cost of a couple KB of ROM space.
This is not compatible with SA-1 as that uses its own thing.

name: smwpatches-optimize-background-tilemap-buffering
title: Optimize Background Tilemap Buffering
description:
This patch optimizes the routine at $058126, which is the routine that decompresses and buffers the layer 2 background tilemap into $7EB900. This routine is incredibly inefficient and can be simplified greatly.

The reduction in load time will vary based on the background used (with no effect for layer 2 levels), but this saved around 248 scanlines loading Yoshi's Island 1 in vanilla (no FastROM, no Lunar Magic, or anything else).

name: smwpatches-per-level-tide-pushback
title: Per-Level Tide Pushback
description:
Allows you to disable the layer 3 tide pushback in specific levels.

Requested by Knight of Time around late 2024/early 2025. I then modified the patch and cleaned it up further, per a request by MrUg123.

name: smwpatches-per-player-straight-fireballs
title: Per-Player Straight Fireballs
description:
This patch will allow you to selectively have straight fireballs in a per-player basis: either for player 1 or for player 2.

Requested by Zack-san.

name: smwpatches-pick-up-sprite-sound
title: Pick Up Sprite Sound
description:
This simple patch adds a sound effect when picking up sprites, like throw blocks, keys, stunned enemies, etc.

Requested by Gamer collin.

name: smwpatches-player-damaging-fireball-flag
title: Player-Damaging Fireball Flag
description:
This patch adds a flag which changes if fireballs interact with sprites or hurt the player.
Affects Yoshi and player fireballs.

If you spawn fireballs via asm, make sure you set the flag to interact with the player or with sprites. If you don't set this flag, it might still be set or not set from the previous sprite.

Requested by Arinsu.

name: smwpatches-player-hp-meter
title: Player HP meter v4.3
description:
This patch will add a health system based on the "numerical HP bar". However its has been heavily edited and added new features by GreenHammerBro:

  • Custom blocks to damage, heal, and increase max HP. Also damage and recovery based on fraction of max HP
  • 16-bit HP and max HP, you can now have up to 65535 HP, Good for hacks that have made collectibles HP upgrades items that are being saved or RPG-styled hacks. Of course, you can change that to 8-bit for HP being less than or equal to 255 to save memory.
  • display HP also as a bar in percentage (based on the HP meter for sprites in the patch section).
  • display HP on overworld border, so the player know how much HP they have without the need to be in a level.
  • All kinds of sprites (normal, custom, cluster, and extended) now have customizable damage, no more several sprites dealing 1HP of damage.
  • perfect knockback, when hit, rather than the need to have higher backward speed, Mario loses control until he's back on the ground. Also, its programmed to knock away from the sprite rather than backwards.
  • Display numerical current HP changes, showing the total damage and recovery briefly.


Read the readme and VersionHistory.txt for more info.

Notes:
  • Bob-omb explosion itself share the damage as the bob-omb, since the explosion is actually the bob-omb sprite.
  • The GIFs here may be rendered at a lower framerate than usual, the bar’s rapid-flicker is a pseudo-transparency effect to display damge or recovery amount.

name: smwpatches-poison-mushroom
title: Poison Mushroom
description:
Applying this patch will specify that an existing sprite number will be a Poison Mushroom instead (ideally an unused one).

Setting the Extra Bit of the sprite in Lunar Magic will make this sprite a kill variant Mushroom. This requires PIXI to be applied to your project.

name: smwpatches-proximity-wraparound-fix-2-0

This patch fixes various sprites using the horizontal and vertical proximity check that wraps around the border of the screen. It includes:

- Thwomps
- Falling spike
- Yoshi egg
- Chargin Chuck
- Splittin Chuck
- Bouncin Chuck

- Rip van fish

name: smwpatches-ram-toggled-spin-jump

description: A more flexible alternative to the tweak to fully disable spin jump (or UberASM that disables the A button) that allows you to disable spin jump on a per-level basis by setting a one-byte FreeRAM flag.

name: smwpatches-random-chance-custom-tile-instead-of
title: Random Chance Custom Tile Instead of 3-up Moon
description:
Makes it so that, during level load, there's a configurable chance a 3-up moon gets replaced by a custom Map16 tile of your liking, subject to normal collectible rules (if you are entering a level where the moon was already collected, nothing will spawn. This is by design).

Includes an example custom block: a blushing in-love moon which grants five extra lives instead of three, complete with custom graphics and ExAnimation.

Dedicated to JerryPKCMoet who inspired the idea via a blushing 3-up moon they made in Minecraft lol

name: smwpatches-replace-cape-with-raccoon
title: Replace Cape With Raccoon
description:
An old patch which replaces Cape Mario for the Raccoon Power-Up through a collection of hex edits and a hijack.

Now properly documented for user-friendlyness' sake, and with fixes to various SFX and visual oversights present in the original version.

Credit to Blargg if used.

name: smwpatches-reznor-fireball-fix-smoke-effect-patch
title: Reznor Fireball Fix + Smoke Effect Patch
description:
This patch allows Reznor to always breathe big fireballs regardless if fought inside a Mode 7 room or not, while also fixing the big fireball's hitbox so it matches its actual size unlike the vanilla game. As a side effect, Jumping Fire-Spitting Piranha Plants can no longer spit huge fireballs under any conditions.

This patch is meant to be a less invasive take to Sonikku's original concept, should you want to fix Reznor's fireballs when used in normal levels and avoid everything else that might cause resource incompatibilities.

As a bonus, it can also add a fancy smoke effect whenever Reznor breathes fire, should the user wish so.

versions.title: Reznor Fireball Fix + Smoke Effect Patch

name: smwpatches-score-sprite-fix-remapper
title: Score Sprite Fix & Remapper
description: This patch allows you to customize the palettes of all score sprites in the game, including the unused 5-up and coin score sprites! Speaking of which, those unused score sprites I just mentioned are totally fixed now and you can separately change the 1-up palette from the 10- to 8,000-point score sprites! Requires 9 bytes of freespace in bank 02, starting from $02D523 by default.

name: smwpatches-smoke-effect-for-bowser-statue-s-fire
title: Smoke Effect for Bowser Statue's Fire
description: This patch adds a simple smoke effect whenever a Bowser Statue breathes fire, not unlike the ones generated by a Bullet Bill shooter.

versions.title: Smoke Effect for Bowser Statue's Fire
versions.filename: Smoke Effect for Bowser Statue%27s Fire 1.1.zip

name: smwpatches-smoother-turn-around-animation
title: Smoother Turn Around Animation
description:
This simple patch makes it so when Mario turns from a standstill or while in the air, he'll face the camera for a few frames, much like he does when holding an item while turning. This makes the animation look a bit smoother.

Originally released on day 4 of Summer C3 2021, but I never submitted it to the section until now.

name: smwpatches-sprite-end-level-scorecard
title: Sprite End Level Scorecard
description:
This patch allows you to replace the layer 3 scorecard with one drawn using sprite tiles, which resolves conflicts with layer 3 briefly disappearing when you clear a level.

Requested by Segment1Zone2.

Mod Note: Doesn't work in the mode 7 boss rooms. Enable the original layer 3 scorecard for those levels specifically.

name: smwpatches-sprite-health-bar
title: Sprite Health Bar
description:
This patch implements a container-based health system in the game. A collectible sprite that increases the amount of containers is also included.
What is different about this patch is that it does not touch the status bar at all, displaying the hearts as sprites instead - in fact, it may be safe to use this along with most of the custom status bar patches available in the site.

There are two ways to use the extra containers:
- It is possible to make them work more akin to SMB2, where they will last for as long as a level (rather than a world in this case), and the original amount of containers will be restored when the player returns to the overworld.
- Like in most games with a health system, the containers can be made to be permanent (this is the default setting). However, you must be careful to assign each of the container sprites an ID via the extra byte, otherwise they will respawn and make it possible to collect infinite containers. The amount of container ID's you can have in total is limited to 16 by default, but this number can be expanded easily with the help of a SRAM/BW-RAM enhancer patch. More information about this can be found in the sprite's .asm file.

Make sure to check the patch's .asm file, as it includes many defines to easily customize, among other things, the graphics and position of the containers. A folder is included with an alternative minimalist design, as well as versions that suit the Mario's 8x8 Tiles DMA-er patch and don't replace occupied SP1-2 tiles.

name: smwpatches-time-to-score-fix
title: Time To Score Fix
description:
Fixes the level end time to score tallying resulting in wrong values when the timer is higher than 400.

Additionally, because tallying higher times would take longer than the level end sequence, it will tally twice as fast for times between 400-799 and thrice as fast for times between 800-999.

name: smwpatches-tolerance-timer-aka-input-buffering-coyote-time
title: Tolerance Timer (aka Input Buffering & "Coyote Time")
description:
This patch aims at making the game's controls more responsive while also lessening the impact of input lag (such as in BSNES or Higan).

So far, two different tricks are supported in the patch and both of them are based on simple timers that add some kind of tolerance window to the game.

The first trick (aka "Coyote Time") allows Mario to perform late jumps. This means that if Mario is about to fall down a platform, as long as a certain amount of time hasn't passed yet, Mario can still perform a jump.

The second trick (aka "Input buffering") basically does the exact opposite to this, as it allows Mario to perform early jumps. This means that if Mario is currently still in the air and pressing a jump button, if he lands on a platform within the next few frames, he will immediately jump off that platform, as if the jump button was pressed the exact moment he landed on it.

By default, both hacks are set to use a frame count of 3 frames (which is equal to about 50 ms of time), but this can be adjusted in the patch. I personally think that 3 frames is a great starting point, but depending on your hack's design, other settings might work even better for you. You can also activate and deactivate both hacks independently from each other. Just take a look at the defines at the top of the patch for details on each setting.

Please play around with the patch for yourself to see how much of a difference it makes, especially in hacks with tight and precise (single block to single block) jumps.

Requires up to 5 bytes of free RAM, depending on which features you enable (3 for late jumps and 2 for early jumps).

Feel free to contribute to this and other patches via my GitHub repository.

name: smwpatches-xorshift-pseudo-random-number-generator
title: Xorshift Pseudo-Random Number Generator
description:
An implementation of the 16-bit variation of a Xorshift linear-feedback shift register algorithm - in particular the (7, 9, 8) variation. Compared to Super Mario World's PRNG, this is:
  • Faster: 72 cycles vs. 96 cycles.
  • Less RAM-consuming: frees 2 bytes of RAM at $148B and $148C.
  • Initialized to a random value on reset (note: most reliable on emulators which have reliable RAM entropy, or hardware).
  • State preserving: RNG does not reset on the overworld.
